extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents and applicants (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to draft and examine patent claims under the Korean Patent Act, including requirements for support by the description, clarity and conciseness, functional/parameter/Markush/composition claim treatment, clerical errors, and independent/dependent claim distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of invention based on claim limitations (applicant’s will)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of the invention for which patent protection is sought shall be made based on the limitations recited in each of the claims in accordance with the applicant’s will. The description or drawings shall be considered only when the claims are indefinite or the definition and meaning of technical terms are ambiguous. The abstract cannot be used to decide the protection scope of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not determine protection scope from the description beyond the claim limitations. Use the description/drawings only to resolve claim indefiniteness or ambiguity of technical terms; never use the abstract to set scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description (Article 42(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be supported by the description of the invention to avoid granting patent rights on subject matter not disclosed to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner determines support by whether a person skilled in the art can figure out subject matter corresponding to the claimed invention from the description (not requiring literal identity). Consider the purport of Article 42(4)(i) and whether the claimed invention departs from the scope grasped by a skilled person based on the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: claim subject matter neither disclosed nor implied in description
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is not supported where the subject matters or limitations of the claims are neither disclosed nor implied in the description of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reciting specific numerical limitations not present in the description; reciting use of an ultrasonic motor when the description only discloses a direct current motor. Exception: if the description indicates other motors can be used and, based on ordinary skill, practicing with the alternative motor is possible, the claim may be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: ambiguous correspondence between claim terms and description terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is not supported where terms used in the claims are different from those used in the description so that correspondence is ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the mapping between claim terms and the description is unclear to a skilled person, support is lacking. Ensure consistent terminology or clear mappings in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: functional means/steps without disclosed specific configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims recite means or steps to perform particular functions but the specific configuration corresponding to such means or steps is not disclosed in the description, the claims lack support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that invoke functional language must be grounded by corresponding structural/configurational disclosure unless the functional language is otherwise made clear by the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: disclosure cannot be extended/generalized to claimed scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are unsupported where the disclosure in the description cannot be extended or generalized to the scope of the claimed invention based on the level of skill in the art at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include claims defined by technical effects (e.g., energy efficiency ranges) where only specific means are disclosed and cannot be generalized, or chemical claims listing many compounds where only a few are shown effective (selective inhibitor example). If ordinary skill cannot recognize that the broader claimed scope is disclosed, support fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: omitting indispensable features described as necessary to solve technical problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that do not recite features explained in the description as indispensable to solve the technical problem are not supported, because a skilled person cannot recognize the claimed invention from the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: description states a specific property (e.g., low water content cream) is required to achieve the effect, but the claim states only 'cream' without the property; the indispensable feature must be claimed or support is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and concise statement of the invention required (Article 42(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must set forth the claimed invention clearly and concisely so they can determine the scope of protection and enable assessment of patentability. This is judged by a person skilled in the art in light of the claims, description, drawings and the level of skill at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conciseness refers to claim language (not the breadth of the inventive idea). Do not rely on parts other than the claims to determine clarity and conciseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: unclear claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is unclear where its language is unclear. However, a mere clerical error that does not lead a skilled person to find the invention unclear (given description/drawings/skill level) is not deemed unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear wording can be resolved by the description or drawings so the invention is understandable by a skilled person, do not find violation. Otherwise, notify ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: listing elements without relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Where each claim element is merely listed but the relationships between the elements are not recited, the invention is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must specify how elements relate; avoid mere enumerations that leave the overall configuration ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: unclear category of claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the category (e.g., product vs method) to which the claimed invention belongs is unclear, the claim is not concise/clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a principle, determine category based on terms/expressions used at the end of the claim; if difficult, deem ambiguous. For products, explain structure/function; for methods, explain steps. Clarify claim endings to indicate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: overly lengthy or repetitive claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim language that is too lengthy, including repetition of the same matter, may render the subject matter unclear and not concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary repetition; craft succinct claim language specifying necessary limitations only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: unclear expressions or vague qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of expressions that make the configuration unclear (e.g., 'at one's will', 'if necessary', 'in particular', 'for example', 'and/or') or vague comparative/degree terms ('mainly', 'appropriate', 'about', 'approximately') or unclear negative limitations ('except for') can render claims unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such expressions cause multiple contrasting inventions to be claimed or ambiguity (e.g., 'and/or'), examine whether description clarifies meaning; otherwise consider ground for rejection. For numerical limitations lacking explicit min/max ('more than', '0~10', dual ranges in one claim) ensure precise numeric bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: unclear subject of indication (reference antecedent issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims become unclear when the indicated subject (antecedent) is ambiguous (e.g., many gears recited and later references like 'said gear' don't specify which).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear antecedent basis and unambiguous reference terms (or explicit reference numerals) so a skilled person can identify the referenced element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: same expression used for different functions without specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple technical terms of the same expression serving different functions are used in the claims without specifying different functions or indicating corresponding reference numerals, the invention is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate identical terms that play different roles (e.g., via reference numerals or explicit function labels) to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: inclusion of irrelevant non-technical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that recite matters irrelevant to technical configuration (e.g., commercial benefits, regions/places of sale) render the invention unclear and not concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude commercial/marketing information from claim language; focus on technical configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not clear/concise: defining by reference to description/drawings without reciting configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims defined solely by reference to the description or drawings without reciting the configuration may be unclear; however, reference is allowed where inevitable (e.g., alloys where special relations cannot be described only in words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reference to drawings only when necessary and ensure the reference permits a skilled person to ascertain the claimed configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical errors: exceptions and examiner handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain clerical errors are not deemed violations of Article 42(4)(ii) and should not be grounds for rejection: (i) 'said OOO' lacking antecedent but invention clear when read excluding 'said'; (ii) slight non-identical terms deemed corresponding by meaning; (iii) claims depending on deleted claims but still understandable when dependencies are adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When clerical errors are present and the invention is clearly understood, the examiner should make an ex officio amendment (if no other rejection grounds exist). If other rejection grounds exist, recommend amendment as 'Matters to be noted' when notifying rejection. If uncertain whether case falls under clerical error, notify ground for rejection to allow applicant response. If after response the claim clearly falls under clerical error, do not reject; make ex officio amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claim requirements (grouping of alternatives not indefinite)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Markush-type claim selecting alternatives from a group does not render the claim indefinite if all inventions configured by selecting an alternative possess a similar property or function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical substances a Markush grouping is acceptable only if (①) all alternatives share a common property/vitality and (②) they share important chemical structure or belong to a group deemed one group in the pertinent art. The same principle may apply in other technical fields (machine, electricity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional limitations: when permitted and examiner determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that include functional limitations reciting a function or effect are not allowed if the configuration is not deemed clear; functional claim language is permitted where (①) defining functionally is necessary because the technical idea cannot be set forth only by configuration (e.g., some biotech or computer-related inventions), or (②) the meaning of the functional limitation is clearly specified by the description or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must determine whether a skilled person can clearly understand the subject matter in light of the description/drawings and the level of skill at filing. If not clear, issue ground for rejection citing Article 42(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product claims defined by manufacturing/process limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A product claim may define the product by the manufacturing method ('product manufactured by the method of...') and is not necessarily indefinite if the product's configuration or nature is clearly understood from the method limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manufacturing method recited in a product claim is unclear even in light of the specification, drawings and ordinary skill at filing, notify rejection under Article 42(4)(ii). If the product's structure/nature cannot be understood from method limitation but the applicant must define by process due to circumstances or proves the process does not affect structure/nature, the examiner may consider the ground remedied and not reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter inventions: when parameter claims are acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameter inventions include parameters arbitrarily created by an applicant (not generally used in the art) or mathematical combinations of variables. Such inventions are generally not clear unless: (①) the technical meaning/definition of the parameter is clearly understood; (②) the inevitable reason for using the parameter is clearly shown; and (③) the relationship with the level of skill at filing is understood in light of the description/drawings and skill level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show the inevitable reason, include comparative examples satisfying and not satisfying the parameter, demonstrating relation between parameter and effect and solving the technical problem. Also include comparative examples for known materials or logical explanation so ordinary skill excludes known materials from the claimed invention. If the parameter's meaning/reason/skill relationship can be understood considering the level of skill at filing even if not explicit, do not deem unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition ratio (%): numeric consistency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims reciting composition ratios as percentages, certain numeric inconsistencies render the claimed configuration unclear: (①) sum of maximum ratios of all components under 100%; ② sum of minimum ratios of all components over 100%; ③ sum of max of one component and mins of others over 100%; ④ sum of min of one component and max of others under 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: composition ranges that logically cannot sum to 100% make the invention unclear. For open claims using 'comprising', some percentage-sum problems may be acceptable because unspecified other components could make 100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open 'comprising' claims can mitigate percentage-sum issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In open claims ('comprising~') which may include unspecified other components, cases where sums would otherwise conflict with 100% (e.g., sum of maxima < 100% or sum of one min + others max <100%) may still be deemed clear because other components can bring total to 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider claim phrasing ('comprising') when evaluating composition percentage consistency; do not automatically reject percentage-sum issues for open claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parts by weight (phrasing) avoids percentage-sum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When composition ratios are described as parts by weight, they do not need to satisfy the percentage-sum requirements applicable to percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts by weight typically indicate relative amounts based on a reference component and allow conversion to relative ratios; such claims are generally considered clear even without a 100% sum check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy claims: composition ranges must sum to 100%
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim directed to an alloy should set forth composition ranges so that the component ranges add up to 100%. Regardless of 'consisting of' or 'comprising', the total sum should not be over or under 100% for alloy claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because alloy properties vary with additives, claims must not only list main components but also recite ranges for other additives as necessary. Example: an alloy claim whose component ranges cannot mathematically reach 100% is unclear and not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should recite matters necessary to specify protection sought (Article 42(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall recite matters regarded necessary to specify what is sought for patent protection, such as structures, methods, functions, materials or combinations thereof. If an invention can be clearly specified, the applicant may choose how to set it forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision itself is not a ground for rejection or invalidation; examiners should not notify rejection based solely on this note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting requirements and multiple-claims system (Enforcement Decree Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The law prescribes how claims are drafted to ensure they determine the scope of protection. Korea adopts multiple claims where one or more claims directed to subject matters may be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formal requirements for claim presentation and numbering to ensure clarity of scope per statutory drafting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination criteria between independent and dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims must narrow or add further limitations to specify an independent claim in terms of content of the invention. A claim that narrows or adds limitations but does not formally refer to the other claim(s) is not a dependent claim; conversely, a claim referring formally to an independent claim but not narrowing/adding limitations is not a dependent claim either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dependent claims both (a) refer to another claim formally and (b) actually narrow or add limitations to that claim. Article 5(1) of the Enforcement Decree requires dependent claims to substantiate the independent claim by narrowing or adding limitations.
